```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("R/setup.R")
```

## Read in the data

All adults (≥ 21 y) with valid height and weight. DXA analyses use the subset with a complete scan.

```{r}
adults     <- read_result("adults")
adults_dxa <- adults |> filter(has_dxa)

cli::cli_alert_info("Adults: {nrow(adults)}; with DXA: {nrow(adults_dxa)}")
record_stat("n_adults", nrow(adults))
```

### Sex and ancestry composition

Ethnicity codes (RIDRETH1): 1 = Mexican American, 2 = Other Hispanic, 3 = non-Hispanic White,
4 = non-Hispanic Black, 5 = Other/multiracial.

```{r}
adults |> count(sex) |> knitr::kable()
adults |> count(ethnicity) |> mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |> knitr::kable()
```

## Log–log regressions of weight on height

The slope of log₁₀W on log₁₀H is the allometric exponent β (Table 1, Equation 3).

### No adjustment for sex

```{r}
fit0 <- lm(log10_weight ~ log10_height, data = adults)
cli::cli_alert_info("R² = {round(summary(fit0)$r.squared, 4)}")
extract_formula(fit0)
```

### Females and males separately

```{r}
fit_by_sex <- adults |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  group_map(~ lm(log10_weight ~ log10_height, data = .x), .keep = TRUE) |>
  set_names(levels(adults$sex))

iwalk(fit_by_sex, function(m, s) {
  cli::cli_alert_info("{s}: R² = {round(summary(m)$r.squared, 4)}")
  extract_formula(m)
})
```

### Sex-adjusted (the model used in Figure 1 and the text)

ΔR² is the share of variance in log₁₀W explained by height after sex (sequential sums of squares).

```{r}
fit <- lm(log10_weight ~ sex + log10_height, data = adults)

beta_adult <- coef(fit)[["log10_height"]]
cli::cli_alert_info("R² = {round(summary(fit)$r.squared, 4)}; ΔR² for height = {round(delta_r2_last(fit), 4)}")
extract_formula(fit)

record_stat("adult_beta_sexadj",     beta_adult)
record_stat("adult_beta_sexadj_3dp", beta_adult)
record_stat("adult_fig1_intercept",  coef(fit)[["(Intercept)"]])
record_stat("adult_fig1_sex_coef",   coef(fit)[["sexMales"]])
```

### Multiplicative (back-transformed) form

W = α × k^sex × H^β, with α = 10^intercept and k = 10^(sex coefficient); sex = 1 for males.

```{r}
alpha_adult <- 10^coef(fit)[["(Intercept)"]]
k_adult     <- 10^coef(fit)[["sexMales"]]

record_stat("adult_fig1_alpha", alpha_adult)
record_stat("adult_fig1_k",     k_adult)

sprintf("W = %.2f × (%.3f)^sex × H^%.3f", alpha_adult, k_adult, beta_adult)
```

## Is BMI independent of height in adults?

If β were exactly 2, log₁₀BMI would not depend on log₁₀H. The slope here equals β − 2.

```{r}
fit_bmi_h <- lm(log10(bmi) ~ sex + log10_height, data = adults)
s_bmi_h   <- summary(fit_bmi_h)$coefficients["log10_height", ]
s_bmi_h

record_stat("adult_bmi_height_b",       s_bmi_h[["Estimate"]])
record_stat("adult_bmi_height_se",      s_bmi_h[["Std. Error"]])
record_stat("adult_bmi_height_p",       s_bmi_h[["Pr(>|t|)"]])
record_stat("adult_bmi_height_dr2_pct", 100 * delta_r2_last(fit_bmi_h), "ΔR² as a percentage")
```

## Figure 1 inputs: fitted lines and binned counts

Panel A shows the log–log model and panel B the back-transformed model, both from the
sex-adjusted fit. Because sex shifts α but not β, there is one line per sex: parallel on the
log scale and proportional on the original scale.

The source data are aggregate: each panel is summarised as counts in a fine 2-D grid. The
individual points are drawn by `figures/fig01_adult_allometry.R` straight from `adults.rds`.

```{r}
### Figure 1A/B: prediction lines from the sex-adjusted model
fig1_lines <- expand_grid(sex    = factor(levels(adults$sex), levels = levels(adults$sex)),
                          height_m = seq(min(adults$height_m), max(adults$height_m), length.out = 200)) |>
  mutate(log10_height = log10(height_m),
         log10_weight = predict(fit, newdata = pick(everything())),
         weight_kg    = 10^log10_weight)                      # conditional median weight

### Figure 1A/B: binned counts (source data only)
bin_counts <- function(x, y, wx, wy) {
  tibble(x = wx * (floor(x / wx) + 0.5), y = wy * (floor(y / wy) + 0.5)) |>
    count(x, y, name = "n")
}
fig1_bins <- bind_rows(
  bin_counts(adults$log10_height, adults$log10_weight, 0.005, 0.01) |> mutate(panel = "A"),
  bin_counts(adults$height_m,     adults$weight_kg,    0.01,  2)    |> mutate(panel = "B")
)

### Equation labels, built from the model (ggtext markup)
fig1_labels <- list(
  A = extract_formula(fit, outcome_label = "log<sub>10</sub> W",
                      labels = c(sexMales = "sex M", log10_height = "log<sub>10</sub> H"),
                      print = FALSE),
  B = sprintf("W = %.2f × (%.3f)<sup>sex</sup> × H<sup>%.3f</sup>",
              alpha_adult, k_adult, beta_adult)
)
fig1_labels

save_result(list(lines = fig1_lines, bins = fig1_bins, labels = fig1_labels,
                 n = nrow(adults)), "res_fig1")
```

For comparison: the v1 Figure 1A line was `geom_smooth(method = "lm")`, i.e. the
**unadjusted** fit `fit0` (slope `r round(coef(fit0)[["log10_height"]], 3)`). The equation
printed on the panel was the sex-adjusted fit (slope `r round(beta_adult, 3)`). v2 draws the
sex-adjusted lines so that the line and the equation agree (DISCREPANCIES B2).

## Adult strata for Figure 2

Decades 21–29 … 60–69 and 70+. Every estimate is adjusted for sex. Points are plotted at the
median age of each stratum.

### Figure 2A (adults): allometric exponent by age

```{r}
beta_adult_strata <- beta_by_stratum(adults, "age_decade", adjust_sex = TRUE)
beta_adult_strata |> knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

### Figure 2B (adults): partial correlation of height with %BF

```{r}
hf_adult_strata <- hf_corr(adults_dxa, "age_decade")
hf_adult_strata |> knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

### Figure 2C (adults): %BF at BMI 25, sex-adjusted GAM

```{r}
curves_adult_adj <- fit_stratum_curves(adults_dxa, "age_decade", adjust_sex = TRUE)
pbf25_adult_adj  <- pbf_at_ref(curves_adult_adj)
pbf25_adult_adj |> select(age_decade, n, age_mid, pbf, lo, hi, p_int) |> knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r}
save_result(list(beta = beta_adult_strata, hf = hf_adult_strata, pbf25 = pbf25_adult_adj),
            "res_adult_strata")
```

## Compositional stability: %BF vs BMI by sex and decade (Figure 8A)

One GAM per sex × decade (`pbf ~ s(bmi, k = 5)`), drawn between the 5th and 95th BMI
percentiles. `sd_resid` (the ribbon in Figure 8A) is the between-person spread in %BF at a
given BMI.

```{r}
curves_adult <- fit_stratum_curves(adults_dxa, "age_decade")
curves_adult |> filter(type == "curve") |> distinct(sex, age_decade, n, age_mid, sd_resid) |> knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

### %BF at BMI 25 by decade (text: compositional stability ¶1)

```{r}
pbf25_adult <- pbf_at_ref(curves_adult)
pbf25_adult |> select(sex, age_decade, pbf, lo, hi, n) |> knitr::kable(digits = 1)

get_pbf <- function(s, g) pbf25_adult |> filter(sex == s, age_decade == g) |> pull(pbf)
record_stat("adult_pbf25_m_2129",  get_pbf("Males",   "21–29"))
record_stat("adult_pbf25_m_70",    get_pbf("Males",   "70+"))
record_stat("adult_pbf25_m_delta", get_pbf("Males",   "70+") - get_pbf("Males",   "21–29"))
record_stat("adult_pbf25_f_2129",  get_pbf("Females", "21–29"))
record_stat("adult_pbf25_f_70",    get_pbf("Females", "70+"))
record_stat("adult_pbf25_f_delta", get_pbf("Females", "70+") - get_pbf("Females", "21–29"))
```

### %BF at reference BMIs 20–35 (input to the drift sweep in 04)

```{r}
pbf_sweep_adult <- pbf_at_ref(curves_adult, opts$ref_bmi_sweep)
pbf_sweep_adult |> count(sex, ref_bmi, name = "n_strata") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = n_strata) |> knitr::kable()

save_result(list(curves = curves_adult, pbf25 = pbf25_adult, sweep = pbf_sweep_adult),
            "res_adult_curves")
```
